title: The Instruction Set Architecture
description: How x86-64 turns bytes into instructions: the mode, the opcode map, the prefix layers, ModRM and SIB, and the length arithmetic a linker needs.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 7 concepts, reproduce the 118 measured checks in courses/isa/assets/samples/crosscheck.py, and decode a code section of a real binary with courses/isa/assets/samples/x86dec.py

concepts.title: One Byte Stream, Two Meanings
concepts.description: 0x40 is INC in one mode and REX in another, so three bytes have two correct readings.

concepts.title: The Opcode Map and Its Holes
concepts.description: 228 of 256 byte values are instructions, 27 are prefixes, and the escape has a deliberately undefined member.

concepts.title: REX: Four Bits That Add Eight
concepts.description: The extension rule that makes R=1 mean r8, and the order rule that makes it the last prefix.

concepts.title: ModRM: The Two Fields That Decide the Length
concepts.description: All 256 combinations, the four mod classes, and the answer to the linker's standing question.

concepts.title: SIB: The Byte That Exists Because rsp Is Special
concepts.description: Scale, index and base, the two field values with special meanings, and a byte order nobody guesses.

concepts.title: The Length Arithmetic
concepts.description: One formula, fourteen specimens, and the chain property that makes a boundary check strong.

concepts.title: Decode It Yourself
concepts.description: An instruction decoder that shows its work, and the table audit that finds what examples miss.
